This R script curates and converts the output file of the CNN segmentation model results in pixel to carbon biomass. 

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

# 1. Load files and libraries
Tasks: Change the directories and file names for df.segmentations and uvp.meta. Make sure the packages are downloaded. ggOceanMaps is useful for mapping but there are other options.
```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Check if any packages need to be downloaded
installed_packages <- c("tidyverse","ggOceanMaps","ggspatial") %in% rownames(installed.packages())
if (any(installed_packages == FALSE)) {
  install.packages(packages[!installed_packages])
}

library(tidyverse)
library(cowplot)
# library(ggOceanMaps)

# An example file of the CNN output
df.segmentations <- read.csv("C:/Sync/UVP6_Data/lipid_predictions_20251123/new_predictions_uvp6_20251123.csv")

# The metadata file of the UVP6 casts
uvp.meta <- read.csv("C:/Sync/UVP6_Data/Alix_Amundsen_Leg5/UVP6_Calanus_metadata_20260129.csv")

# The file of volume of water sampled by the UVP profiles
volumes.df <- read.csv("C:/Sync/UVP6_Data/Alix_Amundsen_Leg5/UVP6_volume_filtered.csv")

`%notin%` <- Negate(`%in%`)
theme_set(theme_bw() +
            theme(text = element_text(size=14)))
```

# 2. Data curation
The main filter for quality control is to remove the predictions with prosome or lipid areas outside the range of values of the manually segmented training dataset (n = 1,808). The range of prosome area in pixels is [249, 3282] and lipid area in pixels is [82, 1730]. We will also exlude two profiles that have unusually low number of Calanus spp.
```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Remove unnecessary columns.
df.segmentations <- df.segmentations %>% 
  # Set the object id to match with the metadata file
  mutate(object_id = str_remove(filename,".png")) %>% 
  filter(object_id %in% uvp.meta$object_id) %>% 
  # Select and rename only the necessary columns
  select(object_id, 
         prosome_pixels = prosome_pixels_predicted, 
         prosome_major = prosome_major_predicted, 
         prosome_minor = prosome_minor_predicted,
         lipid_pixels = lipidpcrop_pixels_predicted, 
         lipid_major = lipidpcrop_major_predicted, 
         lipid_minor = lipidpcrop_minor_predicted) %>% 
  # assign the sample_id of the profile based on the metadata file
  left_join(uvp.meta %>% 
              select(sample_stationid, sample_id, object_id, Depth_5m),
            by = "object_id") %>% 
  relocate(sample_id, object_id, Depth_5m) %>% 
  # exclude some profiles with unusually low number of total images captured
  filter(sample_id %notin% c("am_leg5_TCA_BB2_03", "am_leg5_TCA_T3_17_03"))


# Remove potentially bad segmentation performance. 
df.segmentations <- df.segmentations %>% 
  filter(prosome_pixels >= 249 & prosome_pixels <= 3282) %>% 
  filter(lipid_pixels >= 82 & lipid_pixels <= 1730)

print(paste("N =", nrow(uvp.meta)-nrow(df.segmentations),
            "images were excluded by the outlier filters."))

```

# 3. Convert individual image pixels to area
Derive volume, dry weight, and carbon
```{r, echo=FALSE}
# The UVP6 image resolution 
uvpRes <- 0.073 # mm/pixel
# Conversion factor to get total lipid mg C from total lipid mg used in Schmidt et al. 2018 based on 36-carbon chain lengths in (Kattner & Graeve 1991) 
lambda <- (36*12) / (36*12 + 2*36 + 2*16)
# Conversion factor to get prosome biomass (mg C) from biovolume (mm3)
vol2massC <- mean(c(0.14373,0.1177,0.1902)) # average of 3 Calanus species in (McConville et al. (2016)
# Conversion factor from mm3 -> wet weight -> carbon weight
# If density asssumed as 1, the value below is the Carbon % Wet weight
prosomeWW2C <- 0.09 # 0.09 is the average for all calanoid copepod species


# *** For the CNN segmented images ***
indiv.traits <- df.segmentations %>% 
  
# Calculate traits from pixels
  mutate(lipid_area_mm2 = lipid_pixels * uvpRes * uvpRes,
         prosome_area_mm2 = prosome_pixels * uvpRes * uvpRes,
         prosome_length_mm = prosome_major * uvpRes) %>% 
  # Calculate minor axis based on prosome/lipid area and major axis (in pixels)
  mutate(minor_derived = (prosome_pixels / (pi * prosome_major/2)) * 2) %>% 
    # Calculate biovolume of prosome approximated as spheroid
  mutate(prosome_biovolume_mm3 = 4/3 * pi * 
           (prosome_major/2 * uvpRes) * ((minor_derived/2 * uvpRes)^2)) %>% 
  
  # Calculate lipid sac volume based on Tarling et al. (2022) eq1 derived from Miller et al. (1998) note that this is  based on cyclindrical volume approximation. According to Miller et al. (1998) the oblate spheroid volume approximation is less accurate
  mutate(lipid_volume_mm3 = 
           (pi * lipid_area_mm2 ^ 2)/(4 * lipid_major * uvpRes)) %>% 
  
# (Calculate lipid carbon based on area following Vogedes et al. (2010) with coefficients for 3 Arctic Calanus species
  mutate(totallipid_mass_mg = 0.197 * (lipid_area_mm2 ^ 1.38)) %>%  
  mutate(waxester_mass_mg = 0.167 * (lipid_area_mm2 ^ 1.42)) %>%  
  
  # Calculate lipid carbon mass
  mutate(lipid_mass_mgC = totallipid_mass_mg * lambda) %>%  
  mutate(waxester_mass_mgC = waxester_mass_mg * lambda) %>%  
  
   # Calculate the carbon content of the prosome excluding the lipid sac. Based on Bourreau et al. (in review)
  mutate(structural_carbon_mgC = (prosome_biovolume_mm3 - lipid_volume_mm3) * 
           prosomeWW2C) %>% 
  
  # The total carbon content is the sum of the structural and wax ester carbon
  mutate(prosome_total_mgC = structural_carbon_mgC + waxester_mass_mgC) %>% 
  
  # Calculate lipid fullness as % carbon in lipid sac WE
  mutate(lipid_fullness = waxester_mass_mgC / prosome_total_mgC * 100)
```

## Inspect the distribution of traits for the individuals imaged
```{r, eval=FALSE}
ggplot(indiv.traits,
         aes(x = prosome_length_mm,)) +
    geom_histogram(alpha = 0.7, position = "stack", bins = 50) +
    scale_x_log10(breaks = 2:10, limits = c(1.6, 10)) +
    xlab("Prosome length (mm)") +
    ylab("# Individuals") +
    theme(legend.position = c(0.75, 0.75),
          legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "black"),
          legend.key = element_blank())

ggplot(indiv.traits,
         aes(x = waxester_mass_mgC,)) +
    geom_histogram(alpha = 0.7, position = "stack", bins = 50) +
    # scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.1,0.3,0.5,1,2,3,5)) +
    xlab("Wax ester carbon (mg C)") +
    ylab("# Individuals") +
    theme(legend.position = c(0.75, 0.75),
          legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "black"),
          legend.key = element_blank())

ggplot(indiv.traits,
         aes(x = lipid_fullness)) +
    geom_histogram(alpha = 0.7, position = "stack", bins = 50) +
    xlab("Lipid fullness (% total carbon)") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(30,40,50,60,70,80,90)) +
    theme(legend.position = "none",
          axis.title.y = element_blank())
```



# 4. Calculate abundance and biomass
The data frame of individuals needs to be converted to the abundance and biomass concentrations. The UVP6 data assigns the volume of water sampled in 5 m bins. According to Barth and Stone (2022), the minimum depth bin size for stable concentration estimates is 20 m. Here we can start to explore the data by setting a bin size of 100m, that value can be adjusted if preferred.

Note that some stations can have multiple profiles. For these instances, the profiles are averaged by depth layer. Alternatively, values can be pooled but the resulting estimated concentrations will be similar (Barth and Stone, 2022).
```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Set the size of the depth layers
binsize <- 100 # m

# Calculate the abundance and biomass in 5 m bins (minimum vertical resolution)
df.5m <- indiv.traits %>% 
  # Add column of the volume sampled in 5m depth bins from metadata
  left_join(volumes.df, 
            by = join_by(sample_stationid, sample_id, Depth_5m)) %>% 
  # Calculate total abundance and biomass per 5m bin. Note that this is not yet by volume
  group_by(sample_stationid, sample_id, Depth_5m) %>% 
  summarise(abundance = n(),
         biomass_mgC = sum(prosome_total_mgC),
         structural_mgC = sum(structural_carbon_mgC),
         waxester_mgC = sum(waxester_mass_mgC),
         .groups = "drop") 

# There will be bins sampled by the UVP but with no copepods. This script will fill in the "blank" depth bins when no large Calanus spp copepods were observed.
df.5m.zero <-  volumes.df %>% 
  filter(sample_id %in% df.5m$sample_id) %>% 
  select(-Sampled_volume_L) %>% 
  left_join(df.5m, 
            by = join_by(sample_stationid, sample_id, Depth_5m)) %>% 
  # replace NA with 0
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ replace_na(.x, 0))) 

# Get the total volume sampled for each depth layer in UVP6 profile.
station.profiles <- df.5m.zero %>% 
  mutate(Depth_layer = floor(Depth_5m / binsize) * binsize) %>% 
  # Calculate concentrations per "binsize" m bin (note the number of 5m bins)
  group_by(sample_stationid, sample_id, Depth_layer) %>% 
  summarise(n5mbins = n(),
            Sampled_volume_m3 = sum(Sampled_volume_m3),
            abundance = sum(abundance),
            biomass_mgC = sum(biomass_mgC),
            structural_mgC = sum(structural_mgC),
            waxester_mgC = sum(waxester_mgC),
            .groups = "drop") %>% 
  # This is more ideal because averaging the 5m bin concentrations results in slightly different values because the sampled volume is different per 5m bin
  mutate(abundance_m3 = abundance/Sampled_volume_m3,
         biomass_mgC_m3 = biomass_mgC/Sampled_volume_m3,
         structural_mgC_m3 = structural_mgC/Sampled_volume_m3,
         waxester_mgC_m3 = waxester_mgC/Sampled_volume_m3) %>%
  # To calculate /m2 abundance and biomass by area, multiply by the depth of water sampled which is 5m * the number of 5m bins
  mutate(abundance_m2 = abundance_m3 * (5 * n5mbins),
         biomass_mgC_m2 = biomass_mgC_m3 * (5 * n5mbins),
         structural_mgC_m2 = structural_mgC_m3 * (5 * n5mbins),
         waxester_mgC_m2 = waxester_mgC_m3 * (5 * n5mbins)) %>% 
  
  # Average the concentrations for stations with multiple profiles
  group_by(sample_stationid, Depth_layer) %>% 
  summarise(nprofiles = n(),
            nimages = sum(abundance),
            across(c(abundance_m3:waxester_mgC_m2),
              mean, na.rm = TRUE), 
            .groups = "drop") %>% 
  
  # For visualization purposes, recenter the depth layer
  mutate(Depth_layer = Depth_layer + (binsize / 2)) 


# To calculate the depth-integrated abundance and biomass of each UVP6 profile, simply sum the concentrations by area (m2).
profile.integ <- station.profiles %>% 
  group_by(sample_stationid) %>% 
  summarise(nimages = sum(nimages),
            total_abundance_m2 = sum(abundance_m2),
            total_biomass_mgC_2 = sum(biomass_mgC_m2),
            total_structural_mgC_m2 = sum(structural_mgC_m2),
            total_waxester_mgC_m2 = sum(waxester_mgC_m2),
            .groups = "drop")

rm(df.5m, df.5m.zero)
```


# 5. Visualize the results
## 5.1. Vertical profiles
```{r profiles}
# Abundance concentration
ggplot(station.profiles,
             aes(x = Depth_layer, y = biomass_mgC_m3,
                 fill = sample_stationid)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_x_reverse(breaks = seq(0, 2400, 200), expand = c(0,0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0.01,0.01)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("blue1", "red", "deeppink1","purple2","black",
                               "orange2", "brown", "forestgreen")) +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  xlab("Depth (m)") + ylab("Abundance (indiv m-3)") +
  facet_wrap(~sample_stationid, nrow = 2)

# Biomass concentration
ggplot(station.profiles,
             aes(x = Depth_layer, y = abundance_m3,
                 fill = sample_stationid)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_x_reverse(breaks = seq(0, 2400, 200), expand = c(0,0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0.01,0.01)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("blue1", "red", "deeppink1","purple2","black",
                               "orange2", "brown", "forestgreen")) +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  xlab("Depth (m)") + ylab("Biomass (mg C m-3)") +
  facet_wrap(~sample_stationid, nrow = 2)

```

## 5.2. Spatial map of the depth-integrated values
```{r}
to.plot <- profile.integ %>% 
  # Add the longitude and latitude locations
  left_join(uvp.meta %>% 
              distinct(sample_stationid, .keep_all = T) %>% 
              select(sample_stationid, object_lon, object_lat),
            by = "sample_stationid")


# Prepare the map
basemap("ArcticStereographic", bathymetry = TRUE, glaciers = FALSE,
        limits = c(-82,-50,68,80), rotate = T,
        legends = TRUE, land.col = "#eeeac4",  bathy.style = "poly_grays",
        land.border.col = "black", gla.border.col = NA) +
  # Plot the points
  ggspatial::geom_spatial_point(data = to.plot,
                                aes(x = object_lon, y = object_lat,
                                    # TODO select which variable to plot
                                    color = total_biomass_mgC_2),
                                size = 3,
                                alpha = 1) +
  # Plot the labels
  ggspatial::geom_spatial_text_repel(data = to.plot,
                                aes(x = object_lon, y = object_lat,
                                    label = sample_stationid)) +
  # Improve the visuals
  # TODO make sure to change the variable label and units 
  scale_color_viridis_c(name = "Biomass\n(mg C m-2)") +
  theme(axis.title = element_blank(),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
        legend.position = "right")

```



# 6. Plot Sampling distribution
```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Map the stations using the ggOceanMaps package.
# If you are prompted to download the bathymetry data, enter 1/Yes.
metadata <- uvp.meta %>% 
  distinct(sample_stationid, .keep_all = T)

# Prepare the map
basemap("ArcticStereographic", bathymetry = TRUE, glaciers = FALSE,
        limits = c(-82,-50,68,80), rotate = T,
        legends = TRUE, land.col = "#eeeac4",  bathy.style = "poly_grays",
        land.border.col = "black", gla.border.col = NA) +
  # Plot the points
  ggspatial::geom_spatial_point(data = metadata,
                                aes(x = object_lon, y = object_lat,
                                    color = sample_stationid),
                                size = 3,
                                alpha = 1) +
  # Plot the labels
  ggspatial::geom_spatial_text_repel(data = metadata %>% 
                                       distinct(sample_stationid,
                                                .keep_all = TRUE),
                                aes(x = object_lon, y = object_lat,
                                    label = sample_stationid,
                                    color = sample_stationid)) +
  # Improve the visuals
  scale_color_manual(values = c("blue1", "red", "deeppink1","purple2","black",
                                "orange2", "brown", "forestgreen")) +
  theme(axis.title = element_blank(),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
        legend.position = c(0.88, 0.75)) +
  guides(color = "none") 

# Output figure
# ggsave(filename = "station_map.png",

```
